question.text: Acquiring Company ID trades at INR 540 and Target Company CF trades at INR 39.25 on announcement. The stock-swap merger conversion ratio is 139:10 (139 shares of CF for every 10 shares of ID). What is the fair price of Company ID implied by the conversion ratio and Target's market price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Example 11.7 in Ch 11.2.4.2, fair price of Company ID = (139 x 39.25) / 10 = 5,455.75 / 10 = INR 545.58. Since ID trades at INR 540 in the market, ID is undervalued by INR 5.58 relative to the conversion ratio, so the fund BUYS ID equity. The Trap: Option A uses an incorrect formula direction. Options B and D overshoot the multiplier. The trap is confusing the swap ratio's numerator and denominator. Note: Apply the source formula (139 x 39.25) / 10 to derive INR 545.58 as the implied fair price of ID.
